card: performance/kasei15/poh_benchmarks.json (Navy test of G4M1 aircraft No. 241, Kasei 15)
failing: Rated power, 9,500 kg, brake release to 3,000 m (No. 241: 5 min 27 s)
Rated power, 9,500 kg, brake release to 8,000 m (No. 241: 20 min 18 s)
Rated power, 9,500 kg, 8,000 m to the 9,660 m ceiling (No. 241: 40 min 32 s less 20 min 18 s)
note: Nothing in the airframe or propeller was refitted to No. 241; the level speeds are an out-of-sample pass. The climb above ~6,000 m fails with no sourced fix: the sourced ratings (1,280 hp at 6,000 m, Kasei 11 1,360 hp at 4,100 m) give the Kasei 15 about 16 % more power at 9.6 km on a plain density lapse, 20-25 % in the model, yet No. 241's ceiling was only 140 m above No. 1's. Span-efficiency check: with Raymer's e = 0.81 for AR 7.9 instead of the fitted 0.70, the Kasei 11 card overclimbs near its ceiling (8,000 m to ceiling -27.1 %, 172 against 98 ft/min at 9,520 m; to 3,000 m -4.1 %, to 8,000 m -3.5 %) and the Kasei 15 rows worsen (to 8,000 m -13.0 %, 8,000 m to ceiling -61.2 %, 483 against 98 ft/min), so the excess high-altitude climb is shared by both engines, not the Kasei 15 part: power lapse above the full-throttle height, propeller losses at altitude, or the Navy climb procedure.
known_failure: Known failure, persists after correcting rated_bhp to 2,880 hp (it only changes the reported %BHP): the level speeds pass without fitting while every climb row fails. Leading candidate: propeller compressibility at altitude. The propeller part carries only estimated CT_MACH/CP_MACH tables copied from the P-38G model; a physical compressibility model is parked in Simulate PR #14.
